audit_findings.title: Normalized owner earnings may retain a temporary $316 million pricing-cost timing windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: $316 million pricing-cost timing benefit and $593.4 million inventory cash outflow
audit_findings.mechanism: Raises reported earnings and potentially the OE trend anchor while omitting the associated through-cycle working-capital requirement.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in operating income was driven by the favorable timing of raw material-related pricing compared to costs of approximately $316 million, non-raw material-related pricing and tariff surcharges in Metal Cutting, higher sales and production volumes and incremental year-over-year restructuring savings of approximately $27 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary benefit and inventory outflow are demonstrated by the filing. The $316 million benefit is 2.25 times the $140.4 million anchor, so even partial retention in the log trend is reasonably capable of materially overstating value. The exact anchor error remains unresolved because a timing-adjusted OE series was not supplied.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every affected OE year by removing temporary pricing-cost timing effects, add a normalized tungsten working-capital requirement, recompute the trend anchor, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The June balance-sheet bridge omits an imminent $500 million borrowing whose interest is absent from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $500.0 million expected borrowing; interest and fees unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces projected equity-level OE through interest and fees and affects the cash bridge if borrowed proceeds are incorrectly treated as surplus cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to have fully drawn the $ 500.0 million term loan by September 30, 2026, after which any undrawn commitments will no longer be available.
audit_findings.explanation: The facility and expectation of a full $500 million draw by September 30 are filed facts, but the amount actually drawn by the September 6 valuation date, its rate, fees and use of proceeds are unresolved. The borrowing equals 3.56 times anchor OE, and its recurring financing cost is reasonably capable of materially reducing the cash flow being capitalized.
audit_findings.action: Obtain valuation-date draw confirmations, the term-loan rate and fee schedule, and the proceeds deployment; then project after-tax interest in OE and exclude debt-funded cash from surplus cash before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: The OE numerator may include NCI-owned cash flows while the denominator represents only Kennametal common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.025 million FY2026 NCI income; historical OE correction unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes the historical OE numerator and trend anchor by aligning depreciation, capital expenditure, working capital and other consolidated adjustments with parent ownership.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to Kennametal was $342.4 million, or $4.42 of earnings per diluted share (EPS) in 2026, compared to $93.1 million, or EPS of $1.20 in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The use of parent-attributable income with consolidated OE adjustments is a demonstrated basis inconsistency. FY2026 NCI income was $8.025 million, or 5.7% of the $140.4 million anchor, but that amount does not measure the NCI share of the add-backs and reinvestment. Excess consolidated depreciation could overstate OE while excess consolidated capital expenditure or working-capital deductions could understate it, so net materiality and direction remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each historical OE component to parent ownership, calculate the NCI-attributable share of every add-back and reinvestment item, rebuild the OE series and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: An unresolved litigation claim ahead of equity is not quantified in the valuation
audit_findings.magnitude: initial demand in excess of $330 million; current exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Creates a possible one-time claim against the equity bridge and recurring defense costs or settlement payments that reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: MachiningCloud, Inc. initially sought damages in excess of $ 330 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The litigation is demonstrated, but the filing says the claims and damages were significantly narrowed and provides neither the current demand nor the probability of loss. The initial demand exceeded 16% of the $2.069 billion base equity value, showing potential scale, but it is not a valid estimate of current exposure. The record therefore cannot establish present materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current pleadings or demand, counsel's probability and loss-range assessment, insurance limits and exclusions, and expected defense costs; apply a probability-weighted bridge or scenario adjustment and rerun if warranted.

audit_findings.title: A material uncommenced lease is absent from both historical OE and the reported lease-liability context
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent and operating costs reduce forecast OE; any recognized lease liability would also change lease-obligation context.
audit_findings.evidence: We have signed a material lease agreement related to the Company's future innovation center in Germany.
audit_findings.explanation: The signed lease is demonstrated, but it has not commenced, its payments are excluded from the filed $46.256 million lease liability, and no payment schedule is supplied. It is therefore a forward-looking cost not presently represented in historical OE. Value would be overstated if forecast benefits from the innovation center are recognized without its corresponding occupancy costs.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the executed lease schedule, handover and commencement dates, termination provisions and incremental operating costs; include the costs in forecast OE before crediting related productivity or growth benefits.

audit_findings.title: Pension cash funding may exceed the accounting cost retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.0 million expected 2027 contribution versus $7.277 million FY2026 pension expense, a computed $2.723 million gap; $17.867 million net funded deficit
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces normalized OE when sustainable cash contributions exceed accounting pension expense and may create an additional equity claim where plan surpluses cannot offset underfunded plans.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to contribute approximately $ 10.0 million to our pension plans in 2027, which is primarily for international plans.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed one-year contribution exceeds FY2026 accounting expense by $2.723 million, only 1.9% of the $140.4 million anchor, but a single-year comparison does not establish a persistent normalized shortfall. The aggregate net funded deficit is $17.867 million, or 0.9% of the $2.069 billion base equity value, while the record does not establish whether surplus assets can economically support the substantially underfunded plans. Materiality therefore remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Compile plan-by-plan pension expense, contributions, benefit payments, funded status, statutory funding requirements and surplus-transfer restrictions; substitute normalized unavoidable cash funding for accounting expense and rerun if the persistent difference is material.
